[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/17 (Fri) 12:08  
[USER] User inquired about the potential contribution of Wellbutrin to the risk of serotonin syndrome.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Wellbutrin (bupropion) is not typically associated with an increased risk of serotonin syndrome, as it primarily acts on dopamine and norepinephrine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Caution is needed when combining Wellbutrin with other serotonergic medications.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cymbalta (duloxetine) is the primary serotonergic medication in the patient's medication list.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The risk of serotonin syndrome is relatively low when combining Wellbutrin with Cymbalta, but monitoring is essential.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Serotonin syndrome is a potentially life-threatening condition caused by excessive serotonergic activity in the nervous system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Symptoms of serotonin syndrome may include agitation, confusion, rapid heart rate, and high blood pressure.  
[USER] User asked which medications contribute to serotonin syndrome risk.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cymbalta (duloxetine) is the primary medication associated with an increased risk of serotonin syndrome.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other medications listed do not significantly contribute to the risk of serotonin syndrome on their own.  
[USER] User inquired about trazodone's contribution to serotonin syndrome risk.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Trazodone can contribute to the risk of serotonin syndrome as it is a serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor (SARI).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When combined with other serotonergic medications, such as Cymbalta, the risk of serotonin syndrome can increase.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Symptoms of serotonin syndrome include agitation, confusion, rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, dilated pupils, loss of muscle coordination, muscle rigidity, diarrhea, shivering, sweating, and fever.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Monitoring for signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome is essential, and prompt medical attention is necessary if detected.  
[USER] User requested a mnemonic for serotonin syndrome.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] A mnemonic for recognizing the symptoms of serotonin syndrome is "HARMED":  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] H - Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] A - Autonomic instability: Fluctuations in blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] R - Rigidity: Muscle rigidity or stiffness  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] M - Myoclonus: Rapid, involuntary muscle jerks or twitches  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] E - Encephalopathy: Altered mental status, such
